title: SEO for private equity: an on-site, off-site and technical playbook
summary: A generic SEO checklist for private equity firms. It leans on one stat (SEO leads close at 14.6% vs 1.7% for outbound) and then covers keyword research, on-page basics, backlinks, local and reputation, and technical hygiene. Mostly standard beginner SEO with little original insight.

principles.text: SEO leads close far better than outbound leads because inbound searchers already have intent.
principles.quote: SEO leads have a 14.6% close rate, compared to outbound leads, with a 1.7% close rate

principles.text: Target long-tail keywords: less competitive and more likely to convert into leads.
principles.quote: Long-tail keywords are the more specific phrases that are less competitive and more likely to convert into leads.

principles.text: Optimize content with target keywords but never stuff them; structure it so it is easy to scan.
principles.quote: Include your target keywords and phrases in your content, but avoid keyword stuffing.

principles.text: For backlinks, prioritize quality over quantity: a few reputable links beat many low-quality ones.
principles.quote: It is better to have a few high-quality backlinks from reputable websites than a large number of low-quality backlinks.

principles.text: Prospects research a firm online before committing, so monitor and manage your reputation and reviews.
principles.quote: potential investors will often research a private equity firm online before investing.

principles.text: SEO is ongoing: monitor and adjust the strategy regularly rather than set and forget.
principles.quote: SEO is an ongoing process, and it’s important to monitor and adjust your strategy regularly to stay ahead of the competition.
